Sarah and Daniel welcome you to Grantown-on-Spey, in the beautiful Highlands of Scotland, and to the elegant yet homely Garden Park Guest House. Built in 1868, it is quietly set in half an acre of well-stocked gardens, close to Grantown Golf Course, the Speyside river walk and the pine forests. The High Street, with its family-owned shops, restaurants and pubs, is only a four-minute walk away.
. It connects Strathspey and Badenoch, Speyside, Moray, Nairnshire and the Cairngorms, which makes it one of the best bases for a comfortable, longer stay.

Founded in the 18th century, Grantown is the historical capital of Strathspey and a near-perfect Highland base for day trips, whisky, nature and coast. Since 2003 the town has been part of the Cairngorms National Park, the largest national park in the United Kingdom.

Anagach Woods and the Speyside Way begin minutes from the door, and we are the Guest House closest to the route. Red deer, otters, dolphins, golden eagles, osprey and pine martens all live in the region, and the RSPB centre at Loch Garten is a short drive away.
Nine distilleries and a working cooperage on the Malt Whisky Trail, including The Cairn, Grantown's own distillery. You will find more information on
Eight courses within easy reach, in Grantown, Carrbridge, Boat of Garten, Abernethy, Newtonmore, Kingussie, Aviemore and Craggan. We have lockable storage and drying facilities for clubs and boots.
Ballindalloch Castle, Cawdor Castle and the battlefield at Culloden are all within an hour. Grantown Museum is just around the corner.

We don't serve lunch or dinner, but every booking receives a PDF with all the local restaurants and cafés. Whether you are vegan or love meat or fish, Grantown offers a great variety, and we are always happy to share our personal favourites.
Fishing and stalking can be arranged with a local guide during your stay. Horse riding, pony trekking, birdwatching, skiing, snowboarding and white-water rafting are all nearby.

Grantown-on-Spey is made for staying a little longer. From here, day trips go out in every direction like the points of a star, to Speyside and its distilleries, Aviemore and the Cairngorm mountains, Tomintoul, Elgin, Nairn and the Moray coast, and Inverness, all under an hour away. You unpack once and spend your days exploring instead of packing and driving.

We work closely with Green Tourism and hold their Gold award. Since the 2024 season, solar panels on the south and south-east sides of the house help power Garden Park, and we have replaced all water tanks. If you drive an electric car, you can charge it at our charging station with the Tap Electric app. We also have our own herb garden and a bee-friendly flower garden, buy local where we can, keep packaging and waste low and use steam cleaning where possible.

Every extra night means one less round of washing linen and towels. That saves water and energy, and it keeps detergents out of the wastewater, which has to be treated at great cost and in the end becomes our drinking water again. And it gives you time to really get to know Grantown-on-Spey and the Cairngorms instead of rushing through.

We are open from March to October, and over Christmas and New Year from 26 December to 4 January. From November to February the house is closed, as our old granite house takes a long time to heat. On request, we can open the house in winter for groups of at least six people staying a minimum of three nights.
Bookings are confirmed with a deposit for the first night per room. We accept cash (GBP), bank cards, bank transfer and Stripe payment links, completely contactless.

The house sits slightly raised, about 30 metres from the road, reached by a gentle footpath or by 12 shallow steps. Built in 1868, it is not suitable for wheelchairs. With a rollator or walking aid it works well, and we have already welcomed Guests who use one. Two rooms are on the ground floor, Sutherland with a walk-in shower, Mathieson with a 15 cm shower step.
Travelling with your dog? They are very welcome in Butterfly Cottage, where there is room for the whole family to feel at home. A pet fee of £39 applies per booking, per week.
Drying facilities and lockable storage on site, and we are the Guest House closest to the Speyside Way. Luggage transfer to your next accommodation can be arranged, just ask us before you arrive.

Every room has a complimentary beverage tray, bathroom toiletries, a TV and a hairdryer. You are very welcome to spend time in our residents' lounge, where you'll find board games, books and information about the local area. On colder days, the log-burning stove keeps the room warm and cosy.
